App Review Platform
Internal tools CMS 2022

App
Review
Platform

Ground-up rebuild of Wix App Market’s internal review platform that shortened review cycles.

Overview

TL;DR

  • I planned and rebuilt a stale internal review tool with a clearer structure and the features reviewers were missing.
  • I started with interviews and by shadowing Account Managers as they ran reviews, then tested the redesign with them in a bug hunt before launch.
  • Review cycles got shorter, and the team has used the tool and added features to it since the 2022 launch.
Background

The problem

Account Managers who review apps for the Wix App Market wrote their reviews in different tools: some used Google Docs, others used Sheets. The internal review tool was stuck in a loop: it wasn't updated, so no one used it, and with no one using it, it never got updated.

  • No shared history
  • No visibility into what changed between submissions
  • No consistent handoff between reviewers

As more and more apps were submitted, we noticed that review cycles were long.

App review cycle
Approach

Research

Met with Account Managers to walk through the current system, shadowed them running reviews, audited the Docs and Sheets they used instead, and pulled analytics on time to publish and resubmissions per app. Four pain points came out of it:

A confusing UI

Difficulty writing a consistent review

Weak information architecture

No integrated workflow

Approach

Design principles

Some of the pain points became principles.

Fit the existing workflow.

Reviewers were already working in Docs and Sheets, so the platform had to beat their workaround and feel familiar.

Make every decision traceable.

Every step is logged, and the previous report sits next to the current one.

Show what changed in the app.

A before and after view lets reviewers focus on the delta.

Keep the account managers in control.

Blockers disable publishing, and publishing is always deliberate.

Solution

Redesigning the platform

The main things we solved in the new product.

  • Order. Every step of an app's submission is logged with who did it.
  • Continuity. The previous report sits next to the current one, so a resubmission no longer means digging through an old doc.
  • Consistency. Comments are organized by app path, blockers are flagged inline, and the report is generated automatically.
  • Faster. Changes between submissions show as a before and after column, simple and with nothing new to learn.
  • Scale. One view for all apps at every stage, with search, filters, and status logic built to hold up as submissions grew.
  • New status. Three listing states (Listed, Never Listed, Removed) show each app's market history at a glance.
  • Familiar. Built on Wix's internal UI system instead of a new visual language, answering the confusing UI complaint from research.

Delivery

Delivery and challenges

  • Ran weekly syncs with Account Management to align on scope and surface edge cases early.
  • Ran a bug hunt with Account Managers before launch to validate the redesign.

Challenges

  • Reviewers had already moved to Docs and Sheets, so the platform had to be better than their workaround to win them back.
  • The diff in the second review was not built properly, and the bug hunt is what showed it.
  • Sending the review was still done in a separate Wix platform, because the two systems were not connected.
Results and next steps

Results and impact

Review cycles got shorter. The team stopped working in Google Docs and moved their reviews into the platform, where anyone with permission can follow an app's full history. It has been in use since the 2022 launch, including after AI entered the review process.

Next steps: The team has since added features themselves, such as more filters on the main page and marking an app as premium, which used to need a developer.

The team had already voted with their feet, doing the actual review work in spreadsheets outside the platform. Success wasn't launching a redesign; it was building something good enough that they'd stop reaching for Google Docs. The tool became their primary review surface, which is the only metric that actually mattered.
